name: Fluoxetine
metabolism: Hepatic demethylation, involving CYP2D6 and other pathways, produces active norfluoxetine. Both persist for a long time and undergo further metabolism before predominantly renal elimination of metabolites.
summary: Fluoxetine is a selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor (SSRI) antidepressant used to treat major depressive disorder, anxiety disorders, obsessive-compulsive disorder, panic disorder, premenstrual dysphoric disorder, and bulimia nervosa.
toxicities: DailyMed warnings include suicidal thoughts/behavior (higher risk in children, adolescents, and young adults), serotonin syndrome, seizures, abnormal bleeding, SIADH-associated hyponatremia, QT prolongation and ventricular arrhythmias including torsades, mania/hypomania, and angle-closure glaucoma in susceptible patients.
Commonly reported adverse effects in the cited capsule label include anxiety/insomnia and appetite or weight changes.
generalRisks: The label is for oral fluoxetine capsules (updated 2023-11-28). About suicidality, serotonin syndrome, QT prolongation/ventricular arrhythmias, seizures, bleeding, hyponatremia, mania/hypomania and angle-closure glaucoma. Fluoxetine has long washout constraints around MAOIs; label-specific interactions and formulation limits matter.
saferUse: Seek urgent medical care for suspected serotonin syndrome (agitation or confusion with fever, sweating, tremor, rigidity, or seizure), fainting/palpitations, or suspected overdose.
Monitor for worsening mood or suicidal thoughts, particularly in younger patients and after changes; tell a clinician about seizures, bipolar history, heart rhythm/QT risks, or narrow-angle glaucoma.
Do not combine with MAOIs; follow the specific label washout periods and check before using serotonergic medicines, pimozide, thioridazine, or drugs affecting bleeding.
dosageRemark: The label is a prescription oral capsule label. Its therapeutic regimens are not recreational dose guidance; no recreational threshold or duration is established here.
